content: 1. The effect of pentazocine administered intramuscularly (IM) compared to placebo was assessed in a study. The quality of evidence was rated as low due to a wide confidence interval crossing the line of no effect and a small sample size with few events (<30). The findings were updated for the purpose of this guideline. 2. Tramadol administered intramuscularly (IM) was compared to no analgesia. The effect estimate was derived from a single study with a moderate risk of bias. The quality of evidence was rated as very low due to a wide confidence interval crossing the line of no effect, a small sample size, and few events. 3. Meptazinol administered intramuscularly (IM) was compared to pethidine (IM). The quality of evidence was rated as moderate, with an estimated 59 more events per 1,000 participants (ranging from 14 more to 112 more). The findings were updated for the purpose of this guideline. 4. Morphine or diamorphine administered intramuscularly (IM) was compared to pethidine (IM). The quality of evidence was rated as moderate, with an estimated 12 fewer events per 1,000 participants (ranging from 67 more to 73 fewer). The findings were updated for the purpose of this guideline. 5. Diamorphine administered intramuscularly (IM) plus prochlorperazine was compared to pethidine (IM) plus prochlorperazine. The quality of evidence was rated as very low, with an estimated 28 fewer events per 1,000 participants (ranging from 53 fewer to 104 more). The findings were updated for the purpose of this guideline. 6. Dihydrocodeine administered intramuscularly (IM) was compared to pethidine (IM). The quality of evidence was rated as very low, with an estimated 148 fewer events per 1,000 participants (ranging from 18 more to 256 fewer). The findings were updated for the purpose of this guideline. 7. Pentazocine administered intramuscularly (IM) was compared to pethidine (IM). The quality of evidence was rated as very low, with an estimated 10 fewer events per 1,000 participants (ranging from 94 fewer to 274 more). The findings were updated for the purpose of this guideline. 8. Nalbuphine administered intramuscularly (IM) was compared to pethidine (IM). The quality of evidence was rated as moderate, with an estimated 236 fewer events per 1,000 participants (ranging from 24 fewer to 328 fewer). The findings were updated for the purpose of this guideline. 9. Phenazocine administered intramuscularly (IM) was compared to pethidine (IM). The quality of evidence was rated as low, with an estimated 145 fewer events per 1,000 participants (ranging from 52 fewer to 190 fewer). The findings were updated for the purpose of this guideline. 10. Butorphanol administered intramuscularly (IM) was compared to pethidine (IM). The quality of evidence was rated as very low, with an estimated 17 fewer events per 1,000 participants (ranging from 25 fewer to 174 more). The findings were updated for the purpose of this guideline. 11. Fentanyl administered intravenously (IV) was compared to pethidine (IV). The quality of evidence was rated as very low, with an estimated 11 fewer events per 1,000 participants (ranging from 17 fewer to 145 more). The findings were updated for the purpose of this guideline. 12. Nalbuphine administered intravenously (IV) was compared to pethidine (IV). The quality of evidence was rated as very low, with no events estimable due to a small sample size and no events reported. The findings were updated for the purpose of this guideline. 13. Phenazocine administered intravenously (IV) was compared to pethidine (IV). The quality of evidence was rated as low, with no events estimable due to a small sample size and few events reported. The findings were updated for the purpose of this guideline. 14. Butorphanol administered intravenously (IV) was compared to pethidine (IV). The quality of evidence was rated as very low, with an estimated 0 fewer events per 1,000 participants (ranging from 8 fewer to 128 more).
